tasks.short: Record costs and shipments, check supporting evidence, and post accounting entries.

steps.what: Retrieve shipment and cost records for the posting period.
Read supporting documents and identify missing shipment or cost details.

loop.input: Delivery and cost documents linked to posting source records.
loop.output: Evidence fields with document references and a missing evidence list.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, dates, amounts and duplicate references against source records. Require a source location for each extracted field.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document. Missing, conflicting or unreadable evidence goes to the billing clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured records need no model. Some supporting documents have variable layouts and free text.

steps.what: Assign account codes, cost centres and posting dates.
Compare posting totals with source totals and check duplicate entries.
Resolve mismatches and approve exceptions within delegated accounting limits.
Post approved entries and retain journal references.
File separate copies of posted records and supporting documents.

tasks.design: An integration brings shipment and cost records from the {OPS_SYSTEM} into the {ERP}, where configured rules code entries and check totals. A bounded extraction loop reads supporting documents in the {DOCS}; the {WORKFLOW} routes unresolved evidence and coding exceptions to the billing clerk before posting. Journal references link to retained evidence, removing separate filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records and evidence arrived separately. Small differences in identifiers and document layouts made integration costly.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing posting controls can be configured, while AI coding speeds the connectors and validation code. Bounded extraction handles the remaining document variation.
tasks.still_hard: Missing delivery evidence, disputed costs and unusual accounting treatment still need investigation. Posting permissions and period controls require careful testing.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk establishes what actually happened when shipment records, costs and supporting evidence disagree.

ambition.what: Daily decisions on unresolved shipment-to-ledger differences

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from entry and filing to evidence exceptions and daily reconciliation. With delegated limits, the clerk can clear routine differences sooner; material accounting decisions remain with the accountant.

reach.task: Investigate shipment cut-off differences at period close.
reach.learn: Accruals, cut-off rules and how operational events map to ledger entries.
Record identifiers, data quality measures and reconciliation reporting.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit extracts invoice fields and identifies suppliers. This supports document extraction feasibility, not shipment accounting coverage.
AFAS Profit matches bank lines using record identifiers and sends misses to a person.
Configured coding, control totals and duplicate checks can automate standard postings when source records are reliable.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Most source records are structured, but supporting documents take disproportionate reading time.
The spreadsheet connects operational totals to accounting totals; it is not the primary ledger.
Configured controls can release routine entries under existing delegated authority.
GDPR applies to personal data in evidence. Access is restricted and extraction uses only necessary fields.
Access estimates include checking applicable national consultation rules.
unknowns: Available interfaces and stable shipment identifiers.
Current coding rules, posting limits and materiality thresholds.
Frequency of missing evidence and accounting exceptions.
Whether linked evidence satisfies the customer's retention requirements.
Applicable national employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can the existing {ERP} configure all required coding and reconciliation controls?
Which extraction checks catch document errors before they affect postings?
new_work: Review extracted fields that fail validation.
Investigate missing evidence and conflicting records.
Maintain coding mappings and source identifiers.
Monitor connector failures and duplicate prevention.

tasks.short: Check billing equipment, clear simple faults, and arrange support when needed.

steps.what: Check printer and scanner status in the office-equipment console.
Inspect printer and scanner output for jams, missing pages or poor quality.
Clear simple equipment faults and run a test.
Report unresolved faults and request equipment support.

tasks.design: Configure status alerts in the {OTHER} office-equipment console and route persistent faults to the {HELPDESK} with equipment identifiers. A short form adds the clerk's physical observations and test result, while the {HELPDESK} suppresses duplicate requests. Physical checks and simple repairs stay with the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checking was cheap and equipment status was separate from support records. Physical faults were not fully visible in the console.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing alerts and ticket templates can remove repeated status checking and report writing. AI coding can cheaply connect equipment identifiers where configuration falls short.
tasks.still_hard: A status signal cannot reliably detect every output defect or clear a jam. Older equipment may expose little usable telemetry.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees whether the equipment produces complete, readable billing output and knows when to stop using it.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time checking healthy devices and writing fault reports. Physical troubleshooting and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Summarise equipment downtime affecting billing deadlines.
reach.learn: Fault codes, incident timestamps and how to distinguish repeated alerts from separate failures.

reach.task: Assess whether recurring equipment failures justify replacement.
reach.learn: Downtime costs, service costs and basic replacement appraisal.

evidence.claim: Office-equipment status alerts and templated support requests can reduce routine checking and reporting.
Physical inspection and fault clearing still require a person when devices lack suitable sensors or actuators.

assumptions: Equipment means office printers and scanners used for billing, not industrial plant.
The task remains relevant where physical documents are still handled.
At least some devices already expose status alerts.
Physical inspection dominates more than the supplied screen-heavy prior suggests.
Time shares and remaining percentages are estimates.
The solution monitors equipment, not employee performance.
unknowns: Equipment types and available status interfaces.
Whether equipment monitoring already belongs to a support team.
Frequency and causes of billing equipment failures.
Existing support access and alert permissions.
research_questions: Which faults can existing device alerts detect reliably?
Can existing {HELPDESK} configuration deduplicate equipment incidents?
new_work: Maintain equipment identifiers and support routing.
Add physical observations to unresolved incidents.
Review faults missed by device status signals.

tasks.short: Revise billing manuals after approved rate, rule or regulatory changes.

steps.what: Collect rate amendments, policy changes and regulatory notices.
Compare amendments with current manual sections and list affected instructions.

loop.input: An amendment pack and the current billing manual.
loop.output: Affected sections, proposed changes and source references.
loop.check: Every proposed change must cite an amendment passage and a current manual section. Flag conflicting dates and missing sections.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair pass per amendment pack. Unclear scope goes to the accountant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text amendments and instructions use different wording. Exact text comparison cannot establish the affected sections.

steps.what: Decide applicability, effective dates and required billing treatment.
Revise manual text, rate tables and worked examples.

loop.input: Current manual sections, approved change instructions and approved rate tables.
loop.output: Revised prose and a change log with source references.
loop.check: Code inserts rates and calculates examples. Compare dates, amounts and obligations with approved instructions; reject unsupported additions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per section. Unresolved contradictions return to the billing clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and calculations are deterministic. Explanatory prose needs controlled rewriting across differently worded sections.

steps.what: Approve revised instructions and worked examples for publication.
Publish the approved version and archive superseded instructions.
Notify affected colleagues of changed instructions and effective dates.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} collects amendments from registered sources into the {DOCS} and prepares a cited change map through a bounded reading loop. After the accountant approves applicability, deterministic generators update tables and examples, while a bounded drafting loop revises prose. The financial controller approves the manual before configured versioning and {EMAIL} notifications take effect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manuals mixed rates, examples and prose. Finding every affected passage and preserving approval history took careful manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Document comparison and constrained drafting can prepare revisions. AI coding makes the table generators, validation checks and approval flow cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Regulatory applicability and transitional rules require accountable interpretation. The change must also agree with actual billing configuration.
tasks.human_edge: The accountant decides how a change applies, and the clerk recognises instructions that colleagues could misunderstand.

ambition.what: A billing change impact brief with affected instructions and worked examples

tasks.altitude: Amendment weeks contain less searching and formatting, leaving time to test examples and explain operational effects. The clerk gains responsibility for preparing impact briefs; legal and accounting approval stays with the existing approvers.

reach.task: Prepare an impact brief for a billing rule change.
reach.learn: Source authority, effective dates, transitional provisions and evidence of approval.

reach.task: Validate billing examples affected by tax treatment changes.
reach.learn: Tax applicability and how invoice examples reconcile to approved tax rules.

evidence.claim: Cited document comparison and bounded drafting can prepare manual revisions, while people approve applicability and publication.
EU VAT reforms can require billing procedure changes. Applicability and implementation timing need separate review.
Rate tables and worked examples can be generated and checked deterministically from approved inputs.

assumptions: The manual has an identifiable current version and named approvers.
Regulatory monitoring supplies notices; this design does not establish that every relevant notice has been found.
Time shares include participating approvers and are estimates.
Judgement takes more time than the supplied decision-time prior suggests because applicability and release are distinct decisions.
EU law applies; national billing and employment rules require local interpretation.
Model use requires appropriate AI literacy and GDPR controls where documents contain personal data.
unknowns: Authoritative sources for rate, policy and regulatory amendments.
Who approves legal applicability and manual publication.
Manual formats, version controls and current approval records.
Whether manual revisions are linked to changes in the {ERP}.
Applicable access and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can existing {DOCS} configuration provide versioning and publication approvals?
How should approved examples be checked against the billing configuration?
new_work: Check source references and omissions in change maps.
Review drafted prose for altered meaning.
Maintain rate generators and example checks.
Keep registered sources and notification recipients current.
Verify that published instructions match implemented billing rules.

tasks.short: Weigh paper statement envelopes, determine postage, and apply stamps or metered postage.

steps.what: Weigh prepared statement envelopes on a postal scale.
Look up postage by weight, destination and service.
Affix stamps or apply postage with a postage meter.

tasks.design: Configure statement delivery from the {ERP} through the {EMAIL} for eligible recipients, using validated destinations and recorded delivery preferences in the {WORKFLOW}. This removes weighing and postage for those statements; remaining paper statements use the {OTHER} postage-meter system with configured tariffs. Failed electronic deliveries enter an exception queue for the billing clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper delivery was the established route, and recipient preferences were incomplete. Automating physical envelope handling required equipment investment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing electronic delivery and postage tariff configuration can remove much of the work without robotics. AI coding can cheaply connect delivery preferences, dispatch records and failure handling.
tasks.still_hard: Some recipients need paper, and some statement types may require particular delivery evidence under national rules. Invalid addresses and delivery failures need follow-up.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk identifies recipients who cannot use the normal delivery route and arranges a workable alternative.

ambition.what: Statement delivery assurance for failed electronic deliveries

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer envelopes and more delivery exceptions. With delegated authority, the clerk can select a fallback route after a failed delivery; routine postal spending limits remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve statement delivery failures before starting payment reminders.
reach.learn: Delivery evidence, contact verification and the distinction between non-delivery and non-payment.

reach.task: Validate delivery and retention requirements for statement types.
reach.learn: National notice requirements, accessibility needs and evidence of dispatch.

evidence.claim: Electronic statement delivery removes physical weighing and postage for eligible recipients.
Postage calculation is deterministic when weight, destination, service and current tariffs are known.

assumptions: This describes the paper branch of billing work, which may be small in a mid-size company.
For planning only, 65% of current paper statements are assumed eligible for electronic delivery.
The 35% remaining time for weighing and affixing postage reflects reduced paper volume, not faster physical handling.
A postage meter supports configured tariffs and weight input.
Routine postage uses existing spending authority and needs no separate approval per envelope.
Electronic destinations and delivery preferences are validated before dispatch.
Time shares are estimates. Recipient validation and failed-delivery handling create additional work.
GDPR applies to recipient details and statements. National delivery requirements vary.
Employee consultation is included where national rules require it for the workflow change.
unknowns: Actual paper volume and the share eligible for electronic delivery.
Statement types with mandatory delivery or proof requirements.
Recipient preferences, accessibility needs and address quality.
Available postage equipment and tariff configuration.
Current authority for changing delivery routes and approving exceptional postal costs.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which national rules require paper delivery or retained dispatch proof for these statement types?
Can the existing {ERP} record electronic dispatch and detect failed delivery?
Can existing postage equipment calculate rates without manual tariff lookup?
new_work: Validate recipient destinations and delivery preferences.
Handle failed electronic deliveries and paper fallback.
Update postal tariffs and check unusual charges.
Maintain dispatch evidence and recipient access controls.

role.altitude: The billing clerk spends more time resolving evidence gaps, explaining billing changes and securing statement delivery. Posting exceptions and fallback delivery decisions can be delegated within clear limits; accounting interpretation and material approvals remain with finance approvers.
reach: Help accountants investigate shipment cut-off and reconciliation differences.
Prepare billing change impact briefs with compliance officers.
Help bill and account collectors resolve non-delivery before collection activity.
Work with business intelligence analysts on recurring evidence and delivery failures.
skills_to_grow: Accounting cut-off, coding and reconciliation controls.
Document evidence validation and bounded model-output review.
Regulatory source checking and clear procedural writing.
Delivery evidence, recipient preferences and exception handling.
Basic integration monitoring and data quality reporting.
role.ambitious_version: Become a billing operations analyst who recommends fixes to recurring source-data and delivery problems, tests the billing effects of approved rule changes, and receives delegated authority to clear routine reconciliation and delivery exceptions.
